--- title: "Treemap Visualisation with R" date: "2026-05-10" date-modified: "last-modified" execute: eval: true echo: true warning: false freeze: true --- ## 1. Overview In this hands-on exercise, I will gain hands-on experience designing treemaps using appropriate R packages. The exercise consists of three main sections. First, I will manipulate transaction data into a treemap structure using selected functions from the **dplyr** package. Then, I will plot static treemaps using the **treemap** package. In the third section, I will design interactive treemaps using the **d3treeR** package. ## 2. Installing and Launching R Packages I will first check and load the **treemap**, **treemapify**, and **tidyverse** packages. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pacman::p_load(treemap, treemapify, tidyverse) ``` ::: ## 3. Data Wrangling In this exercise, I will use the *REALIS2018.csv* data, which provides information on private property transaction records in 2018. The dataset is extracted from the REALIS portal of the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA). ### 3.1 Importing the Data Set I will use *read_csv()* of **readr** to import realis2018.csv into R and parse it into a tibble data frame. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} realis2018 <- read_csv("Hands-on Exercises/Hands-on W5/realis2018.csv") ``` ::: ### 3.2 Data Wrangling and Manipulation The *realis2018* data frame is in transaction record form — highly disaggregated and not appropriate for plotting a treemap. I will perform the following steps: - Group transaction records by *Project Name*, *Planning Region*, *Planning Area*, *Property Type*, and *Type of Sale*. - Compute *Total Unit Sold*, *Total Area*, *Median Unit Price*, and *Median Transacted Price* by applying appropriate summary statistics. I will use two key **dplyr** verbs: *group_by()* and *summarise()*. *group_by()* breaks down a data frame into specified groups of rows, after which verbs are automatically applied "by group". *summarise()* computes the summary for each group. ### 3.3 Grouped Summaries without the Pipe The code chunk below shows a two-line approach to perform the steps. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} realis2018_grouped <- group_by(realis2018, `Project Name`, `Planning Region`, `Planning Area`, `Property Type`, `Type of Sale`) realis2018_summarised <- summarise(realis2018_grouped, `Total Unit Sold` = sum(`No. of Units`, na.rm = TRUE), `Total Area` = sum(`Area (sqm)`, na.rm = TRUE), `Median Unit Price ($ psm)` = median(`Unit Price ($ psm)`, na.rm = TRUE), `Median Transacted Price` = median(`Transacted Price ($)`, na.rm = TRUE)) ``` ::: ::: callout-note Aggregation functions such as *sum()* and *median()* follow the usual rule of missing values — if there's any missing value in the input, the output will be missing. The argument `na.rm = TRUE` removes missing values prior to computation. ::: ### 3.4 Grouped Summaries with the Pipe A more efficient way to tackle the same process is using the pipe `%>%`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} realis2018_summarised <- realis2018 %>% group_by(`Project Name`, `Planning Region`, `Planning Area`, `Property Type`, `Type of Sale`) %>% summarise(`Total Unit Sold` = sum(`No. of Units`, na.rm = TRUE), `Total Area` = sum(`Area (sqm)`, na.rm = TRUE), `Median Unit Price ($ psm)` = median(`Unit Price ($ psm)`, na.rm = TRUE), `Median Transacted Price` = median(`Transacted Price ($)`, na.rm = TRUE)) ``` ::: ## 4. Designing Treemap with treemap Package The **treemap** package is specially designed to offer great flexibility in drawing treemaps. The core function *treemap()* offers at least 43 arguments. In this section, I will explore the major arguments for designing elegant and truthful treemaps. ### 4.1 Designing a Static Treemap In this section, I will use *treemap()* to plot a treemap showing the distribution of median unit prices and total unit sold of resale condominiums by geographic hierarchy in 2018. First, I will filter records belonging to resale condominium property type: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} realis2018_selected <- realis2018_summarised %>% filter(`Property Type` == "Condominium", `Type of Sale` == "Resale") ``` ::: ### 4.2 Using the Basic Arguments The code chunk below designs a treemap using the three core arguments: *index*, *vSize*, and *vColor*. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} treemap(realis2018_selected, index = c("Planning Region", "Planning Area", "Project Name"), vSize = "Total Unit Sold", vColor = "Median Unit Price ($ psm)", title = "Resale Condominium by Planning Region and Area, 2018", title.legend = "Median Unit Price (S$ per sq. m)" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands_on_Ex05_5_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=1440} ::: ::: Things to note: - `index`: the index vector must consist of at least two column names, otherwise no hierarchy treemap will be plotted. The first name is the highest aggregation level. - `vSize`: the column must not contain negative values, as its values map to the sizes of the rectangles. ::: callout-warning The treemap above was wrongly coloured. For a correctly designed treemap, the colours of the rectangles should be in different intensities showing median unit prices. Without defining `type`, *treemap()* assumes `type = index`, meaning it colours by the hierarchy of planning areas. ::: ### 4.3 Working with vColor and type Arguments I will now define the `type` argument as `"value"` for correct colouring: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} treemap(realis2018_selected, index = c("Planning Region", "Planning Area", "Project Name"), vSize = "Total Unit Sold", vColor = "Median Unit Price ($ psm)", type = "value", title = "Resale Condominium by Planning Region and Area, 2018", title.legend = "Median Unit Price (S$ per sq. m)" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands_on_Ex05_5_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=1440} ::: ::: The rectangles are now coloured with different intensities of green, reflecting their respective median unit prices. The legend shows values binned into ten equal intervals of 5,000. ### 4.4 Colours in treemap Package Two arguments determine the mapping to colour palettes: *mapping* and *palette*. The `"value"` treemap treats the palette as diverging (e.g. `"RdYlBu"`), mapping 0 to the middle colour, while `"manual"` maps min(values) to the left-end colour and max(values) to the right-end colour. ### 4.5 The "value" Type Treemap ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} treemap(realis2018_selected, index = c("Planning Region", "Planning Area", "Project Name"), vSize = "Total Unit Sold", vColor = "Median Unit Price ($ psm)", type = "value", palette = "RdYlBu", title = "Resale Condominium by Planning Region and Area, 2018", title.legend = "Median Unit Price (S$ per sq. m)" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands_on_Ex05_5_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=1440} ::: ::: Note that although the `RdYlBu` palette is used, there are no red rectangles — because all median unit prices are positive. ### 4.6 The "manual" Type Treemap The `"manual"` type maps the value range linearly to the colour palette: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} treemap(realis2018_selected, index = c("Planning Region", "Planning Area", "Project Name"), vSize = "Total Unit Sold", vColor = "Median Unit Price ($ psm)", type = "manual", palette = "RdYlBu", title = "Resale Condominium by Planning Region and Area, 2018", title.legend = "Median Unit Price (S$ per sq. m)" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands_on_Ex05_5_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-9-1.png){width=1440} ::: ::: The colour scheme is confusing here because a diverging palette like `RdYlBu` is not wise when all values are positive. I will use a single colour palette instead: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} treemap(realis2018_selected, index = c("Planning Region", "Planning Area", "Project Name"), vSize = "Total Unit Sold", vColor = "Median Unit Price ($ psm)", type = "manual", palette = "Blues", title = "Resale Condominium by Planning Region and Area, 2018", title.legend = "Median Unit Price (S$ per sq. m)" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands_on_Ex05_5_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=1440} ::: ::: ### 4.7 Treemap Layout *treemap()* supports two popular treemap layouts: `"squarified"` and `"pivotSize"`. The default is `"pivotSize"`. The squarified algorithm (Bruls et al., 2000) produces good aspect ratios but ignores sorting order, while the pivot-by-size algorithm (Bederson et al., 2002) takes sorting order into account. ### 4.8 Working with algorithm Argument The code chunk below plots a squarified treemap: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} treemap(realis2018_selected, index = c("Planning Region", "Planning Area", "Project Name"), vSize = "Total Unit Sold", vColor = "Median Unit Price ($ psm)", type = "manual", palette = "Blues", algorithm = "squarified", title = "Resale Condominium by Planning Region and Area, 2018", title.legend = "Median Unit Price (S$ per sq. m)" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands_on_Ex05_5_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){width=1440} ::: ::: ### 4.9 Using sortID When `"pivotSize"` algorithm is used, the `sortID` argument determines the order in which rectangles are placed from top-left to bottom-right. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} treemap(realis2018_selected, index = c("Planning Region", "Planning Area", "Project Name"), vSize = "Total Unit Sold", vColor = "Median Unit Price ($ psm)", type = "manual", palette = "Blues", algorithm = "pivotSize", sortID = "Median Transacted Price", title = "Resale Condominium by Planning Region and Area, 2018", title.legend = "Median Unit Price (S$ per sq. m)" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands_on_Ex05_5_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){width=1440} ::: ::: ## 5. Designing Treemap using treemapify Package **treemapify** is specially developed to draw treemaps in **ggplot2**. Before getting started, I recommend reading the [Introduction to treemapify](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/treemapify/vignettes/introduction-to-treemapify.html) and its [user guide](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/treemapify/treemapify.pdf). ### 5.1 Designing a Basic Treemap ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data = realis2018_selected, aes(area = `Total Unit Sold`, fill = `Median Unit Price ($ psm)`), layout = "scol", start = "bottomleft") + geom_treemap() + scale_fill_gradient(low = "light blue", high = "blue") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands_on_Ex05_5_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png){width=1440} ::: ::: ### 5.2 Defining Hierarchy **Group by Planning Region:** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data = realis2018_selected, aes(area = `Total Unit Sold`, fill = `Median Unit Price ($ psm)`, subgroup = `Planning Region`), start = "topleft") + geom_treemap() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands_on_Ex05_5_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){width=1440} ::: ::: **Group by Planning Area:** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data = realis2018_selected, aes(area = `Total Unit Sold`, fill = `Median Unit Price ($ psm)`, subgroup = `Planning Region`, subgroup2 = `Planning Area`)) + geom_treemap() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands_on_Ex05_5_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png){width=1440} ::: ::: **Adding boundary lines:** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data = realis2018_selected, aes(area = `Total Unit Sold`, fill = `Median Unit Price ($ psm)`, subgroup = `Planning Region`, subgroup2 = `Planning Area`)) + geom_treemap() + geom_treemap_subgroup2_border(colour = "gray40", size = 2) + geom_treemap_subgroup_border(colour = "gray20") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands_on_Ex05_5_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png){width=1440} ::: ::: ## 6. Designing Interactive Treemap using d3treeR ### 6.1 Installing d3treeR Package *d3treeR* is not available on CRAN. I will install it from GitHub as follows: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Step 1: Install devtools if not already installed install.packages("devtools") # Step 2: Load devtools and install d3treeR from GitHub library(devtools) install_github("timelyportfolio/d3treeR") ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(d3treeR) ``` ::: ### 6.2 Designing an Interactive Treemap The code below performs two steps: **Step 1:** I use *treemap()* to build a treemap using selected variables, saving the result as ***tm***. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tm <- treemap(realis2018_summarised, index = c("Planning Region", "Planning Area"), vSize = "Total Unit Sold", vColor = "Median Unit Price ($ psm)", type = "value", title = "Private Residential Property Sold, 2018", title.legend = "Median Unit Price (S$ per sq. m)" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands_on_Ex05_5_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-19-1.png){width=1440} ::: ::: **Step 2:** I use *d3tree()* to build an interactive treemap from the *tm* object. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} d3tree(tm, rootname = "Singapore") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: :::
